question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Diminish
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Weaken.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Diminish" is a verb which means to make or become less, smaller or weaker; to reduce in size, strength, importance or intensity. (कम होना / घटाना / कमज़ोर करना)

◦ Its closest synonym among the options is "weaken", which also means to make less strong or less powerful.

◦ Example: Regular exercise diminishes/weakens the risk of heart disease, and long illness diminished his strength.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Demote" means to lower someone in rank or position (पदावनत करना) — it applies to a person's post, not to a general reduction. Its antonym is "promote".

• Option 2 "Relegate" means to push down to a lower/inferior position or category (निम्न स्थान पर भेजना), e.g., a football club is relegated to a lower division. It is not a general synonym of "diminish".

• Option 3 "Prevent" means to stop something from happening (रोकना) — stopping is not the same as reducing gradually.

NOTE

• Synonyms of diminish: decrease, lessen, weaken, dwindle, wane, abate, subside, curtail, shrink.

• Antonyms of diminish: increase, enlarge, augment, amplify, expand, magnify.

• Frequently asked SSC pair: "diminishing returns" (ह्रासमान प्रतिफल) — an economics term meaning progressively smaller gains from each extra unit of input.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A person who loves or collects books
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Bibliophile.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Bibliophile" is a person who loves, reads or collects books. (पुस्तक-प्रेमी)

◦ Word formation: Greek biblio- = "book" + -phile = "one who loves". So biblio + phile = book-lover.

◦ Example: A true bibliophile, she owned first editions of every novel she admired.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Anglophile" = a person who admires England, the English people or English culture (Anglo = English).

• Option 2 "Heliophile" = a person (or plant) that loves or thrives in sunlight (helio = sun).

• Option 3 "Paedophile" = a person who is abnormally/criminally attracted to children (paedo = child) — a negative term that does not fit here.

NOTE

• Other "-phile" words often asked in SSC exams: Bibliophile (books), Cinephile (films), Francophile (France), Audiophile (high-quality sound), Oenophile (wine), Xenophile (foreigners).

• Related words: Bibliography (a list of books consulted), Bibliomania (an obsessive craze for collecting books), Bibliotheca (a library or book collection).

• The opposite is Bibliophobe (one who hates or fears books).

question:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error.

(A) We are living / (B) here since / (C) the summer / (D) of last year.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. A.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Part (A) "We are living" contains the error. When an action began at a point in the past and is still continuing, and the sentence uses "since", the correct tense is the present perfect continuous — "has/have been + V-ing" — not the present continuous.

◦ Incorrect: We are living here since the summer of last year.

◦ Correct: We have been living here since the summer of last year.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Part (B) "here since" is correct — "since" is properly used with a point of time (the summer of last year).

• Part (C) "the summer" and Part (D) "of last year" are grammatically correct noun phrases indicating that point of time.

NOTE

• Rule: With "since / for" expressing duration up to the present, use the Present Perfect or Present Perfect Continuous, never the Present Continuous or Simple Present.

◦ "I have been waiting for two hours." (NOT "I am waiting for two hours.")

◦ "She has known him since 2015."

• since + point of time (since Monday, since 5 o'clock, since 2019, since last summer).

• for + period of time (for two hours, for three years, for a long time).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Suresh has been learning Tamil ________ two months.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. for.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is followed by "two months", which is a period/length of time, not a point of time. With a period of time in the present perfect continuous we use the preposition "for".

◦ Correct: Suresh has been learning Tamil for two months.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "from" indicates a starting point and is normally paired with "to/till" (from Monday to Friday); it is not used with the present perfect to show duration.

• Option 2 "since" is used only with a point of time — "since June", "since Monday", "since two months ago". "Since two months" alone is wrong.

• Option 3 "before" means earlier than a given time and does not express continuing duration.

NOTE

• Golden rule: for + length of time (for two months, for five years, for a while); since + point of time (since 2020, since morning, since he left).

• Both are used with the Present Perfect / Present Perfect Continuous tense: "He has worked here for ten years" / "He has worked here since 2014".

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.

Rina’s house is at a stone’s throw from the school.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. A very short distance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "a stone's throw (away)" means a very short distance; very near/close by — literally, as far as one could throw a stone. (बहुत कम दूरी पर / पत्थर फेंकने की दूरी पर)

◦ Correct sense: Rina's house is very close to the school.

◦ Example: The hotel is just a stone's throw from the railway station.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "A very long distance" is the exact opposite of the idiom's meaning.

• Option 2 "Next to" means immediately adjoining/adjacent, which is stronger and more literal than the idiom — a stone's throw means nearby, not necessarily touching.

• Option 4 "Not very close to" again reverses the sense.

NOTE

• Other idioms meaning "very near": "within spitting distance", "a hop, skip and a jump away", "round the corner", "at hand".

• Idioms meaning "very far": "at the back of beyond", "the ends of the earth", "a far cry from".

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Accompanyment.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Accompanyment" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "accompaniment" — meaning something that goes along with or supplements another thing, or the musical support played behind a singer. (संगत / साथ में दी जाने वाली वस्तु)

◦ Spelling key: AC + COM + PA + NI + MENT. When the suffix "-ment" is added to "accompany", the final -y changes to -i: accompany → accompaniment.

◦ Example: Rice is the usual accompaniment to this curry. / She sang to the accompaniment of a piano.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Wrestler" (a person who wrestles — पहलवान) is correctly spelt: W-R-E-S-T-L-E-R (silent "w").

• "Debatable" (open to argument or dispute — बहस योग्य) is correctly spelt; the final "e" of "debate" is dropped before "-able".

• "Discrepancy" (a difference or inconsistency between two things — विसंगति/अंतर) is correctly spelt: DIS + CREP + AN + CY.

NOTE

• Rule: A word ending in a consonant + y changes y → i before most suffixes: accompany → accompaniment, happy → happiness, marry → marriage, beauty → beautiful.

• Exception: keep the "y" before "-ing" — accompanying, marrying, studying.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Mohan unknowingly altered salt instead of sugar to the dessert making it taste terrible.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. added salt instead of sugar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb must fit the structure "___ something TO the dessert". Only "add" collocates with "to" in this sense — "added salt to the dessert". "Add" means to put one thing together with another. (मिलाना / डालना)

◦ Correct: Mohan unknowingly added salt instead of sugar to the dessert, making it taste terrible.

◦ The context (the dessert "tastes terrible") confirms that salt was put into the dish by mistake.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Altered" means changed or modified (बदलना). One does not "alter salt to a dessert" — the phrase is grammatically and semantically wrong.

• Option 2 "Anguished" means caused severe mental pain / to be in agony (पीड़ा देना) — it cannot take "salt" as an object.

• Option 3 "Amplified" means made larger, louder or stronger (बढ़ाना, विशेषकर ध्वनि) — used for sound or effect, not for putting an ingredient into food.

• Option 4 "Abridged" means shortened/condensed (संक्षिप्त करना), used of books, speeches, texts.

NOTE

• Useful collocations: add something to something; mix something with something; sprinkle something on/over something; pour something into something.

• Distinguish: adopt (to take up/accept), adapt (to adjust), adept (skilled), add (to put in) — a very common SSC confusion set.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

The actor decided to live life in the fast lane.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. A life filled with excitement.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "(life) in the fast lane" means an exciting, eventful and often risky or extravagant lifestyle, full of activity, glamour and pleasure. (रोमांच और उत्तेजना से भरा जीवन)

◦ Correct sense: The actor decided to live an exciting, glamorous and eventful life.

◦ Example: After winning the lottery he began living life in the fast lane — parties, travel and fast cars.

• The expression comes from the "fast lane" of a motorway, used by the quickest vehicles; figuratively it stands for a hectic, high-pressure, thrill-filled way of living.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Dropping charges of crime" has nothing to do with the idiom — it is a legal expression.

• Option 3 "Racing away to the moon" is a literal, invented phrase, not the idiomatic meaning.

• Option 4 "A life of extreme speed" is the literal reading of "fast lane". Idioms must be interpreted figuratively, so this is a distractor — the idiom refers to excitement and glamour, not to physical speed.

NOTE

• Related idioms: "live it up" (enjoy oneself lavishly), "paint the town red" (celebrate wildly), "burn the candle at both ends" (exhaust oneself with too much activity).

• Its opposite is "life in the slow lane" — a quiet, relaxed, unhurried way of living.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

Sanjana rubbed her eyes hardly.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. hardly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Hardly" does not mean "in a hard manner"; it is an adverb of degree meaning "scarcely / almost not at all". The sentence intends to say that she rubbed her eyes with force, so the correct adverb is "hard".

◦ Incorrect: Sanjana rubbed her eyes hardly. (= she almost did not rub them)

◦ Correct: Sanjana rubbed her eyes hard.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Sanjana" (subject), "rubbed" (correct past tense of "rub") and "her eyes" (object) are all correct.

• Words like hardly, scarcely, barely, rarely, seldom are negative adverbs — they already carry a negative sense, so no extra "not" is used with them: "He can hardly speak" (NOT "He cannot hardly speak").

NOTE

• Similar adjective/adverb pairs where the "-ly" form changes meaning completely:

◦ hard (with effort) vs hardly (scarcely) — "He works hard" / "He hardly works".

◦ late (not early) vs lately (recently).

◦ near (close) vs nearly (almost).

◦ most (the greatest amount) vs mostly (mainly).

• Structure point: "hardly ... when", "scarcely ... when" and "no sooner ... than" are followed by inversion — "Hardly had she left when it began to rain".

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

I asked my friend to ___________________ against her employers who are doing wrong to her.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. fight fire with fire.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "fight fire with fire" means to respond to an attack by using the very same methods/tactics that one's opponent is using. (जैसे को तैसा जवाब देना / ईंट का जवाब पत्थर से देना)

◦ The context — employers who "are doing wrong to her" — shows that the friend is being treated unfairly and is being advised to hit back with the same weapons.

◦ Correct: I asked my friend to fight fire with fire against her employers who are doing wrong to her.

◦ Example: When his rivals spread rumours about him, he decided to fight fire with fire.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Fine words butter no parsnips" is a proverb meaning mere talk/flattery achieves nothing; action is needed. It is a complete saying and cannot be slotted after "to".

• Option 2 "Finders keepers, losers weepers" is a children's saying meaning whoever finds something is entitled to keep it. It is irrelevant here and is also a full sentence.

• Option 3 "Fight the good fight" means to strive persistently for a worthy moral cause; it is normally used absolutely (not with "against" a person) and lacks the "retaliate in kind" sense demanded by the context.

NOTE

• Related idioms of retaliation: "give someone a taste of their own medicine", "an eye for an eye", "tit for tat", "pay someone back in their own coin".

• Note the fixed form: "fight fire with fire" — the preposition never changes.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains a misspelt word.

The single most important factor that distinguishes those of us who succed in any venture and those of us who don’t is this ‘instant coffee’ attitude.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. succed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Succed" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "succeed", a verb meaning to achieve the aim or result one wanted; to prosper. (सफल होना)

◦ Spelling key: SUC + CEED — double "c" and double "e" (-ceed, not -ced).

◦ Correct: ... those of us who succeed in any venture ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Distinguishes" (from distinguish — to recognise or show the difference between things; अंतर करना) is correctly spelt.

• "Venture" (a risky or daring undertaking, an enterprise; उद्यम/जोखिम भरा कार्य) is correctly spelt.

• "Attitude" (a settled way of thinking or feeling; दृष्टिकोण) is correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Only three English verbs end in "-ceed": succeed, proceed, exceed. One ends in "-sede": supersede. All the rest end in "-cede": precede, recede, concede, secede, intercede, accede.

• Word family of succeed: success (noun), successful (adjective), successfully (adverb), succession, successor, successive.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

A night alone / in a hotel / can be lonely prospect.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. can be lonely prospect.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Prospect" is a singular countable noun, so it must be preceded by a determiner (article). The indefinite article "a" is missing before "lonely prospect".

◦ Incorrect: ... can be lonely prospect.

◦ Correct: ... can be a lonely prospect. ("a" is used because "lonely" begins with the consonant sound /l/.)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "A night alone" is correct — the article "a" is properly used with the singular countable noun "night".

• "in a hotel" is correct — "in" is the right preposition of place and "a" is the correct article.

• "No error" cannot be chosen because a definite error (the missing article) exists.

NOTE

• Article rule: Every singular countable noun needs a determiner — a/an, the, this/that, my/his, one, etc. "He is doctor" ✗ → "He is a doctor" ✓.

• Use a before a consonant sound (a university, a one-rupee coin) and an before a vowel sound (an hour, an MBA, an honest man).

• "Prospect" here means the possibility or expectation of something happening (संभावना).

question:
Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. One of them contains an error. The underlined parts are given as options with some changes. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.

The new restaurant on Main Street is cheap than the old one.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. is cheaper than.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "than" is a signal of the comparative degree. "Cheap" is a short adjective, so its comparative is formed by adding -er → "cheaper".

◦ Incorrect: The new restaurant on Main Street is cheap than the old one.

◦ Correct: The new restaurant on Main Street is cheaper than the old one.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "the older one" is wrong — the sentence compares the new restaurant with the already existing ("the old one"); changing it to "the older one" does not remove the actual grammatical error, which lies in "is cheap than".

• Option 2 "in Main Street" is unnecessary — the standard American/neutral usage for a named street with an address on it is "on Main Street"; the original is acceptable.

• Option 3 "newer restaurant" is wrong — no comparison of newness is being made, and "the new restaurant" is already correct.

NOTE

• Degrees of comparison: cheap – cheaper – cheapest; big – bigger – biggest; happy – happier – happiest.

• One-syllable and some two-syllable adjectives take -er/-est; longer adjectives take more/most (more expensive, most expensive).

• Never use a double comparative ("more cheaper") or a comparative without "than" when a comparison is intended.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

My relatives shall have reached Amritsar by now.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. shall.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence expresses a strong assumption/logical certainty about a completed action — "by now they have surely arrived". For such a presumption, the correct modal is "must" (or "will/should"), not "shall".

◦ Incorrect: My relatives shall have reached Amritsar by now.

◦ Correct: My relatives must have reached Amritsar by now.

• "Shall" with the third person ("my relatives") expresses command, promise, threat or determination, which is clearly not the intended meaning here.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "My" is a correct possessive adjective before the noun "relatives".

• "Reached" is the correct past participle used after "have"; note that "reach" is used without a preposition before a place — "reached Amritsar" (NOT "reached at Amritsar").

• "By now" is a correct adverbial phrase used with perfect forms to mean "before this moment".

NOTE

• Modals of deduction (present/past):

◦ must have + V3 = certain that it happened ("He must have left").

◦ may/might have + V3 = possible that it happened.

◦ can't have + V3 = certain that it did not happen.

• Traditional rule: shall with I/We for simple future; will with He/She/They/You. Reversing them adds the sense of determination, promise or command.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

Group of bees
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Swarm.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "swarm" is the correct collective noun for bees (and for other flying insects such as flies, locusts and gnats). (मधुमक्खियों का झुंड)

◦ Correct: A swarm of bees attacked the intruders.

◦ "Swarm" also works as a verb: "Bees swarmed around the hive."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Gaggle" is the collective noun for geese (on the ground); geese in flight form a "skein".

• Option 2 "Shoal" is used for fish (also "school of fish").

• Option 4 "Pack" is used for wolves, dogs or hounds (also a pack of cards).

NOTE

• Common collective nouns asked in SSC exams: a swarm of bees, a flock of sheep/birds, a herd of cattle, a pride of lions, a troop of monkeys, a school/shoal of fish, a litter of puppies, a pack of wolves, a fleet of ships, a bunch of keys/grapes, a galaxy of stars, a bevy of girls, a catalogue of books.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Crude
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Refined.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Crude" means raw, unprocessed, unpolished; or rude, vulgar and lacking sophistication. (कच्चा / असंस्कृत / अशिष्ट)

◦ Its antonym is "refined", meaning purified/processed or cultured, polished and elegant in manner. (परिष्कृत)

◦ Example: Crude oil is processed in a refinery to give refined petroleum products. / His crude jokes shocked the refined audience.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "Primitive" (belonging to an early, undeveloped stage — आदिम) is a synonym, not an antonym, of crude.

• Option 1 "Patient" (able to endure delay calmly — धैर्यवान) and Option 4 "Observant" (quick to notice things — प्रेक्षणशील) are unrelated to the meaning of crude.

NOTE

• Synonyms of crude: raw, unrefined, coarse, rough, vulgar, rudimentary, primitive.

• Antonyms of crude: refined, polished, cultured, sophisticated, processed, elegant.

• Static link: Crude oil is the unprocessed petroleum extracted from the earth; India's largest crude refinery is at Jamnagar, Gujarat.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Can you quote any _______ in your favour?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. precedent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "precedent" is an earlier event, decision or case that is regarded as an example or rule to be followed in similar situations later (especially in law). (पूर्व-उदाहरण / नज़ीर)

◦ The verb "quote" collocates naturally with "precedent" — one quotes/cites a precedent to support one's own position, which matches "in your favour".

◦ Correct: Can you quote any precedent in your favour?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "answer" does not fit — one gives an answer, one does not "quote an answer in one's favour".

• Option 2 "summary" (a short account of the main points) is not something quoted to support an argument.

• Option 3 "lines" is too vague; "quote a few lines" is possible, but "any lines in your favour" is unidiomatic and does not convey supporting authority.

NOTE

• Word family: precedent (noun — an earlier example), precede (verb — to come before), preceding (adjective — coming before), unprecedented (adjective — never done or known before).

• Legal usage: courts "set a precedent", "follow a precedent" or "overrule a precedent". In India, under Article 141, the law declared by the Supreme Court is binding on all courts — the doctrine of precedent (stare decisis).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Assasin.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Assasin" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "assassin" — a person who murders an important or famous person, usually for political or religious reasons. (हत्यारा — विशेषकर किसी प्रमुख व्यक्ति का)

◦ Spelling key: AS + SAS + SIN — there are two pairs of "s" (a-s-s-a-s-s-i-n), and the word ends in "-sin".

◦ Example: The assassin was arrested within hours of the killing.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Insurance" (an arrangement giving financial protection against loss — बीमा) is correctly spelt.

• "Mischievous" (naughty; causing trouble — शरारती) is correctly spelt; note there is no "i" after the "v" — it is mischiev-ous, NOT "mischievious".

• "Inexpressible" (too great or intense to be described in words — अवर्णनीय) is correctly spelt with the suffix "-ible".

NOTE

• Word family: assassin (noun — the killer), assassinate (verb), assassination (noun — the act).

• The word comes from Arabic hashshashin, a medieval sect said to have carried out political murders.

• Other frequently misspelt SSC words: accommodation, occurrence, embarrassment, questionnaire, millennium, harass, committee.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Buying a new car can cost an arm and a leg.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Be expensive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "cost an arm and a leg" means to be extremely expensive; to cost a very large amount of money. (बहुत महँगा होना)

◦ Correct sense: Buying a new car can be very expensive.

◦ Example: That designer handbag cost her an arm and a leg.

• The image behind the idiom is that the price is so high that one would have to give up one's limbs to pay it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Be free" (costing nothing) is the exact opposite.

• Option 2 "Be affordable" (within one's means) and Option 3 "Be reasonable" (not too costly) both contradict the idiom.

NOTE

• Other idioms about high cost: "cost a fortune", "cost a pretty penny", "pay through the nose", "break the bank", "daylight robbery".

• Idioms about low cost: "dirt cheap", "a steal", "for a song", "cost next to nothing".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Insist
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Persist.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Insist" means to demand or state something firmly and refuse to give way; to keep pressing for something. (आग्रह करना / ज़ोर देना)

◦ Its closest synonym here is "persist", which means to continue firmly in an opinion or course of action in spite of opposition. (डटे रहना / लगे रहना)

◦ Example: She insisted on paying the bill and persisted until we agreed.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Resist" means to oppose or withstand (विरोध करना) — it is close to the opposite of insisting on something.

• Option 3 "Heist" means a robbery or burglary (डकैती) — a noun, completely unrelated.

• Option 4 "Assist" means to help (सहायता करना) — unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of insist: persist, urge, press, demand, maintain, assert, emphasise, stress.

• Prepositions: "insist on/upon something" (She insisted on going) and "insist that + clause" (He insisted that she come).

• Word family: insistent (adjective), insistence (noun); persistent (adjective), persistence (noun).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

There are several reasons why people might 1)_________ that homework is an unnecessary burden on children. Firstly, there is evidence to support the idea that homework 2)_________nothing to improve educational outcomes. Countries such as Finland, where school children are not given homework, regularly top international educational league tables and outperform nations where setting homework is the norm. Secondly, many parents would agree that the school day is already 3)_________, and leaves their children too tired to do further study when they return home. 4)_________, it is recognised that play time is just as 5)_________as study time from the perspective of brain development.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. argue.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank follows the modal verb "might" ("people might ______ that homework is ..."). Every modal auxiliary (can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, must) is followed by the bare infinitive (V1) — the base form of the verb without "to" and without any -s/-ed/-ing ending.

◦ Correct: There are several reasons why people might argue that homework is an unnecessary burden on children.

• "Argue" here means to put forward reasons in support of a view; to contend. (तर्क देना)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "be argues" is doubly wrong — a finite "-s" form cannot follow "be", and "be" cannot follow "might" with a main verb attached this way.

• Option 2 "have argue" is wrong — after "have" the past participle (V3) is required ("have argued"), not the base form.

• Option 3 "argues" is wrong — the "-s" form is used only with a third-person singular subject in the simple present, and never after a modal.

NOTE

• Rule: Modal + V1 (bare infinitive). "She can swim", "You must go", "He might come".

• Contrast the perfect modal: modal + have + V3 — "He might have argued".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

There are several reasons why people might 1)_________ that homework is an unnecessary burden on children. Firstly, there is evidence to support the idea that homework 2)_________nothing to improve educational outcomes. Countries such as Finland, where school children are not given homework, regularly top international educational league tables and outperform nations where setting homework is the norm. Secondly, many parents would agree that the school day is already 3)_________, and leaves their children too tired to do further study when they return home. 4)_________, it is recognised that play time is just as 5)_________as study time from the perspective of brain development.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. does.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject of the blank is "homework", an uncountable (singular) noun. By the rule of subject–verb agreement, a singular subject in the simple present takes the "-s" form of the verb — hence "does".

◦ Correct: ... evidence to support the idea that homework does nothing to improve educational outcomes.

• The expression "do nothing to + verb" means to have no effect at all in bringing something about.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 4 "do" is the plural form and would need a plural subject ("homeworks" is not used in English; homework is always uncountable).

• Option 1 "will does" is wrong — after the modal "will" only the bare infinitive can follow ("will do").

• Option 2 "has do" is wrong — after "has" the past participle is required ("has done").

NOTE

• Uncountable nouns that are commonly mistaken for plurals and always take a singular verb: homework, information, furniture, advice, luggage, machinery, news, equipment, scenery, poetry, stationery.

◦ "The news is encouraging." / "This information is correct." / "Homework does not always help."

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

There are several reasons why people might 1)_________ that homework is an unnecessary burden on children. Firstly, there is evidence to support the idea that homework 2)_________nothing to improve educational outcomes. Countries such as Finland, where school children are not given homework, regularly top international educational league tables and outperform nations where setting homework is the norm. Secondly, many parents would agree that the school day is already 3)_________, and leaves their children too tired to do further study when they return home. 4)_________, it is recognised that play time is just as 5)_________as study time from the perspective of brain development.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. long enough.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence complains that the school day already takes up so much time that children come home "too tired to do further study". The adjective that describes the duration of a day is "long", and the adverb "enough" is correctly placed after the adjective.

◦ Correct: ... the school day is already long enough, and leaves their children too tired to do further study when they return home.

• The clue words "already" and "too tired" confirm the sense of sufficient (indeed excessive) length.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "big enough" is wrong — "big" refers to size, not to the length of time of a school day.

• Option 3 "not enough" reverses the meaning; it would suggest the school day is too short, contradicting "too tired to do further study".

• Option 4 "enough of" needs a following noun ("enough of the work") and cannot stand alone here.

NOTE

• Placement rule for "enough":

◦ After adjectives/adverbs — "old enough", "fast enough", "long enough".

◦ Before nouns — "enough money", "enough time".

• Contrast with "too": "too + adjective (+ to-infinitive)" shows excess in a negative sense — "too tired to study".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

There are several reasons why people might 1)_________ that homework is an unnecessary burden on children. Firstly, there is evidence to support the idea that homework 2)_________nothing to improve educational outcomes. Countries such as Finland, where school children are not given homework, regularly top international educational league tables and outperform nations where setting homework is the norm. Secondly, many parents would agree that the school day is already 3)_________, and leaves their children too tired to do further study when they return home. 4)_________, it is recognised that play time is just as 5)_________as study time from the perspective of brain development.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Finally.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage lists reasons in a clear sequence of discourse markers: "Firstly, there is evidence ... Secondly, many parents would agree ... ______, it is recognised that play time is ...". The blank introduces the last item in the list, so the linker required is "Finally". (अंत में / आख़िरकार)

◦ Correct: Finally, it is recognised that play time is just as beneficial as study time from the perspective of brain development.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Similarly" shows likeness between two ideas, but this sentence introduces a new and final reason, not a parallel one.

• Option 2 "Normally" and Option 4 "Usually" are adverbs of frequency/habit; they do not signal the closing item of an enumeration.

NOTE

• Sequencing linkers: Firstly / First of all → Secondly → Thirdly → Then / Next → Finally / Lastly / In conclusion.

• Other linker families useful for SSC cloze tests: contrast (however, nevertheless, on the contrary), addition (moreover, besides, furthermore), cause–effect (therefore, hence, consequently), example (for instance, namely).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

There are several reasons why people might 1)_________ that homework is an unnecessary burden on children. Firstly, there is evidence to support the idea that homework 2)_________nothing to improve educational outcomes. Countries such as Finland, where school children are not given homework, regularly top international educational league tables and outperform nations where setting homework is the norm. Secondly, many parents would agree that the school day is already 3)_________, and leaves their children too tired to do further study when they return home. 4)_________, it is recognised that play time is just as 5)_________as study time from the perspective of brain development.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. beneficial.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure "as + adjective + as" is used to show equality. The sentence compares play time with study time "from the perspective of brain development", so the adjective must be a positive one — "beneficial", meaning favourable, advantageous, producing good results. (लाभदायक)

◦ Correct: ... it is recognised that play time is just as beneficial as study time from the perspective of brain development.

• The whole paragraph argues in favour of less homework and more play, so a word of praise is required.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "soon" is an adverb of time and cannot describe play time in this comparison of value.

• Option 3 "bad" reverses the writer's argument — the passage is defending play time, not criticising it.

• Option 4 "confidential" (meant to be kept secret — गोपनीय) is completely out of context.

NOTE

• Comparison of equality: as + adjective/adverb + as → "as beneficial as", "as tall as", "as quickly as". The negative form may use "not so ... as".

• Word family: benefit (noun/verb), beneficial (adjective — advantageous), beneficiary (noun — one who receives a benefit), benefactor (noun — one who gives help).
